item.title: Canada Student Visa, Attestation Letter (PAL) and New Rules 2024
item.dc:creator: bipin.sharma
item.content:encoded:
Are you dreaming of studying in Canada? Well, you're not alone. Canada is known for its world-class education system, diverse culture, and stunning landscapes. But first, you need to navigate the process of obtaining a student visa. Don't worry, we've got you covered. In this complete guide, we will walk you through the ins and outs of the Canada student visa application process, requirements, and opportunities available to international students. YouTube Video - Canada Student Visa from OFFER STAGE to VISA STAGE: [embed]https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=H5QUPUaEDQk[/embed] From selecting the right study program, choosing a reputable institution, to preparing the necessary documents, we will provide you with all the information you need to unlock your dream of studying in Canada. Our step-by-step guide will ensure that you follow the correct procedures, avoid common pitfalls, and increase your chances of obtaining a student visa. Not only will we guide you through the visa process, but we will also explore the incredible opportunities that await you in Canada. From part-time work options to post-graduation work permits, Canada offers a wealth of opportunities for international students to gain practical experience and launch their careers. So, let's dive in and unlock the doors to your Canadian education dreams!

Why choose Canada for your education?

Canada has consistently been ranked as one of the top destinations for international students. With its high-quality education system, diverse multicultural society, and post-study work opportunities, it's no wonder students from all over the world flock to Canada for their education.

One of the key reasons to choose Canada for your education is the reputation of its institutions. Canadian universities and colleges are known for their academic excellence and rigorous standards. Whether you're interested in pursuing a degree in engineering, business, arts, or any other field, you can be assured that you will receive a quality education that is recognized worldwide.

In addition to the quality of education, Canada is also known for its welcoming and inclusive society. As an international student, you will have the opportunity to experience a multicultural environment where you can learn from people of different backgrounds and cultures. This exposure will not only enrich your educational experience but also broaden your horizons and enhance your global perspective.

Furthermore, Canada's stunning landscapes and vibrant cities offer a high standard of living, making it an attractive destination for students seeking a well-rounded educational experience. From the bustling streets of Toronto to the natural wonders of Banff National Park, Canada offers a diverse range of experiences that will make your time as a student truly unforgettable.

Understanding the application process for Offer Letter

Before you can apply for a student visa, you need to receive an offer letter from a Canadian Designated Learning Institution (DLI). The offer letter serves as proof that you have been accepted into a program of study in Canada. To understand the application process for the offer letter, follow these steps:

  1. Research and select the right study program: Start by exploring the different study programs offered by Canadian institutions. Consider your career goals, interests, and academic strengths when selecting a program. Research the admission requirements, curriculum, and faculty to ensure it aligns with your educational aspirations.
  1. Choose a reputable institution: Once you have decided on a study program, research and choose a reputable Canadian institution that offers the program. Consider factors such as the institution's ranking, reputation, faculty expertise, and facilities. It's important to select an institution that meets your academic and personal needs.
  1. Prepare the necessary documents: Each institution will have specific documentation requirements for the application process. Generally, you will need to provide academic transcripts, proof of English language proficiency (such as IELTS or TOEFL scores), letters of recommendation, a statement of purpose, and a valid passport. Make sure to check the institution's website for the exact document requirements.

Once you have gathered all the necessary documents, you can proceed with the application process for the offer letter. Most institutions have an online application portal where you can submit your documents. Pay attention to any deadlines and ensure that you provide accurate and complete information in your application. Some colleges or universities require application fees to process for the offer letter. Make sure you pay the application fees.

Receive an Offer of Admission

Upon acceptance into a program at a Designated Learning Institute (DLI), you will receive an offer letter. The offer letter includes all the information such as program name, program duration, total tuition fees, program start date, program completion date, etc. You need to accept the offer letter and pay a tuition deposit or one-year fees in order to receive letter of acceptance (LOA). This document is essential for your visa application and must be included in your submission to prove your acceptance into a Canadian educational program.

Eligibility requirements for a Canada student visa

To be eligible for a Canada student visa, you must meet certain requirements set by the Government of Canada. These requirements ensure that you are a genuine student and have the financial means to support yourself during your stay in Canada. Here are the key eligibility requirements:

  1. Acceptance into a Designated Learning Institution (DLI): To apply for a student visa, you must have a letter of acceptance from a DLI in Canada. A DLI is a school, university, or college that is authorized by the Canadian government to host international students.
  1. Proof of financial support: You must demonstrate that you have sufficient funds to cover your tuition fees, living expenses, and return transportation. The exact amount of funds required may vary depending on the location and duration of your study program. It's important to provide accurate and up-to-date financial documents, such as bank statements or loan approval letters.
  1. Health and character requirements: You must undergo a medical examination to prove that you are in good health and not a danger to public health in Canada. Additionally, you must provide a police clearance certificate or similar documentation to demonstrate that you have a clean criminal record.
  1. Immigration documents: You will need a valid passport to apply for a student visa. Make sure your passport is valid for the duration of your intended stay in Canada. You may also be required to provide additional documents, such as biometrics (fingerprints and photograph) and a completed application form.

Meeting these eligibility requirements is crucial to the success of your student visa application. It's important to carefully review the requirements and ensure that you provide all the necessary documents in the correct format.

Document checklist for a Canada student visa application

When applying for a Canada student visa, it's important to have all the necessary documents in order to avoid any delays or rejections. Here is a checklist of the documents you will typically need for a student visa application:

  1. Valid passport: Ensure that your passport is valid for the duration of your intended stay in Canada. If your passport is near expiration, consider renewing it before applying for a student visa.
  1. Letter of acceptance: Provide the original or a copy of your letter of acceptance from a Designated Learning Institution (DLI) in Canada.
  1. Proof of financial support: Demonstrate that you have sufficient funds to cover your tuition fees, living expenses, and return transportation. This can be done through bank statements, scholarship letters, or loan approval letters.
  1. Academic transcripts: Include your academic transcripts from previous educational institutions. These transcripts should be official and provide a record of your academic achievements.
  1. Language proficiency test results: If English or French is not your first language, you may need to provide test results from a recognized language proficiency test, such as IELTS or TOEFL.
  1. Medical examination certificate: Undergo a medical examination with an approved panel physician and provide the certificate of completion.
  1. Police clearance certificate: Obtain a police clearance certificate or similar documentation to demonstrate that you have a clean criminal record.
  1. Additional documents: Depending on your specific circumstances, you may be required to provide additional documents, such as proof of job experience, marriage certificates, or birth certificates.

It's important to note that the document requirements may vary slightly depending on the specific visa office or country you are applying from. It's advisable to consult the official website of the Canadian visa office in your country for the most up-to-date and accurate information.

How to apply for a Canada student visa?

Once you have gathered all the necessary documents, you can proceed with the application process for a Canada student visa. The application process typically involves the following steps:

  1. Apply online or on paper: You can apply for a student visa online through the Government of Canada's official website (IRCC) or by submitting a paper application at the nearest visa application center. The online application process is usually faster and more convenient.
  1. Pay the application fee: There is a non-refundable application (CAD 150) fee that you must pay when submitting your student visa application. The fee varies depending on the country you are applying from.
  1. Submit your documents: Upload or mail all the required documents as per the specific instructions provided in the application form. Make sure to include all the necessary supporting documents and complete the application form accurately.
  1. Biometrics collection: Depending on your nationality, you may be required to provide biometrics (fingerprints and photograph) as part of the application process. You will receive instructions on how and where to provide your biometrics. Generally, your biometric is collected via VFS Global if your country don't have Embassy. You need to book an appointment to go to VFS. If you are wondering how to book a VFS appointment, you can simply follow the tutorials in this YouTube Video. You need to pay CAD 85 as a biometric collection charge.
  1. Attend an interview (if required): In some cases, you may be asked to attend an interview at the visa office or consulate. The purpose of the interview is to assess the genuineness of your application and clarify any doubts or concerns.
  1. Wait for the decision: After submitting your application, you will need to wait for the visa office to process your application. The processing time can vary depending on the workload of the visa office and other factors. You can check the estimated processing times on the official website of the Government of Canada.

Once your application is approved, you will receive PPR and a letter of introduction or a temporary resident visa (TRV) if required. This document will allow you to travel to Canada and obtain your study permit at the port of entry.

Study permit processing time and fees

The processing time for a study permit can vary depending on various factors such as the visa office, time of year, and complexity of your application. On average, the processing time for a study permit is around 8 to 10 weeks. However, it's important to note that this is just an estimate, and the actual processing time may be shorter or longer.

When applying for a study permit, you will also need to pay an application fee. As of the time of writing this article, the fee for a study permit is CAD 150. In addition to the application fee, you may also need to pay for biometrics collection, medical examinations, and other associated costs.

It's important to budget for these fees and factor them into your overall financial plan. Make sure to check the official website of the Government of Canada for the most up-to-date information on study permit processing times and fees.

Working while studying in Canada

One of the major advantages of studying in Canada is the opportunity to work while pursuing your education. As an international student, you can work on or off-campus without a separate work permit. Here are some key points to know about working while studying in Canada:

  1. On-campus work: As an international student, you are allowed to work on-campus at the institution where you are enrolled. There are no restrictions on the number of hours you can work. On-campus jobs can include positions such as research assistants, library assistants, or student ambassadors.
  1. Off-campus work: International students are also allowed to work off-campus for up to 20 hours per week during regular academic sessions and full-time during scheduled breaks, such as summer or winter holidays. This allows you to gain practical work experience and supplement your income while studying.
  1. Co-op and internships: Many Canadian institutions offer co-op programs and internships that allow students to gain valuable work experience related to their field of study. These programs typically involve alternating periods of study and work, providing a balance between theoretical knowledge and practical skills.
  1. Post-graduation work permit (PGWP): After completing your studies, you may be eligible for a post-graduation work permit (PGWP). The PGWP allows you to work in Canada for up to three years, depending on the length of your study program. This provides an excellent opportunity to gain Canadian work experience and potentially transition to permanent residency.

Working while studying in Canada can not only help you financially but also provide valuable work experience that can enhance your career prospects. It's important to familiarize yourself with the specific work permit regulations and restrictions to ensure compliance with the Canadian immigration laws.

Post-graduation work permit (PGWP)

The post-graduation work permit (PGWP) is an excellent opportunity for international students to gain valuable work experience in Canada after completing their studies. The PGWP allows you to work in Canada for up to three years, depending on the length of your study program. Here are some key points to know about the PGWP:

  1. Eligibility requirements: To be eligible for a PGWP, you must have completed a full-time study program at a Designated Learning Institution (DLI) in Canada. The program must be at least eight months in duration and lead to a degree, diploma, or certificate.
  1. Length of the PGWP: The length of the PGWP depends on the length of your study program. If your program is between eight months and two years, you may be eligible for a PGWP equal to the length of your program. If your program is two years or longer, you may be eligible for a three-year PGWP.
  1. Application process: To apply for a PGWP, you must submit an application to the Government of Canada. The application must be submitted within 180 days of receiving your final marks or graduation. You will need to provide proof of completion of your study program, a valid passport, and any other supporting documents required.
  1. Work opportunities with a PGWP: With a PGWP, you can work for any employer in Canada and are not limited to a specific job or industry. This provides you with the flexibility to gain work experience in your chosen field and explore different career opportunities.
  1. Permanent residency pathway: The PGWP can also serve as a pathway to permanent residency in Canada. By gaining Canadian work experience, you can potentially qualify for various immigration programs, such as the Canadian Experience Class (CEC), which prioritize candidates with Canadian work experience.

The PGWP is an excellent opportunity for international students to gain valuable work experience and potentially transition to permanent residency in Canada. It's important to plan your career goals and take advantage of the work opportunities available to you during your study period and with a PGWP.

Conclusion and next steps

Congratulations! You have now unlocked the doors to your Canadian education dreams. By following the steps outlined in this guide, you are well on your way to obtaining a Canada student visa and embarking on an incredible educational journey.

Remember to carefully research and select the right study program and institution that aligns with your career goals and interests. Gather all the necessary documents and ensure that you meet the eligibility requirements for a student visa. Follow the application process diligently, paying attention to deadlines and providing accurate information.

Once you have obtained your student visa, take advantage of the incredible opportunities that await you in Canada. Work on or off-campus to gain practical experience and supplement your income. Consider participating in co-op programs or internships to further enhance your skills and employability. And after completing your studies, explore the post-graduation work permit (PGWP) and potential pathways to permanent residency.

Studying in Canada is not just about gaining a world-class education. It's about immersing yourself in a multicultural society, exploring stunning landscapes, and building connections that will last a lifetime. So, go ahead, unlock your dream, and embrace all the opportunities that Canada has to offer!

Now that you have a complete guide to the Canada student visa and opportunities, it's time to take the next steps. Research the study programs and institutions that interest you, start gathering the necessary documents, and begin the application. Good Luck!

item.title: USA Student Visa Process: Complete Guide for Nepali Students
item.dc:creator: bipin.sharma
item.content:encoded:
Navigating the process of obtaining a USA student visa can be overwhelming, especially for Nepali students. This comprehensive guide will walk you through all the steps of USA student visa process, ensuring you have all the information needed to achieve your dream of studying in the United States. Watch YouTube Video Step-by-Step USA Student Visa Process:  [embed]https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tAtBUlBejo8&t=5s[/embed]

Table of Contents

1. Understanding the USA Student Visa Types 2. Step-by-Step Process to Apply for a USA Student Visa - Step 1: Research and Select Your Program - Step 2: Apply to U.S. Institutions - Step 3: Receive Your I-20 Form - Step 4: Pay the SEVIS Fee - Step 5: Complete the DS-160 Form - Step 6: Schedule Your Visa Interview - Step 7: Attend the Visa Interview - Step 8: Receive Your Visa and Prepare for Departure 3. Tips for a Successful Visa Application 4. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) 5. Conclusion

Understanding the USA Student Visa Types

F-1 Visa

The F-1 Visa is the most common type of student visa for those pursuing academic studies at a U.S. college or university.

J-1 Visa

The J-1 Visa is for exchange visitors participating in programs that promote cultural exchange, including studying, training, or research.

M-1 Visa

The M-1 Visa is for students attending vocational or technical schools.

Step-by-Step USA Student Visa Process

 

Step 1: Research and Select Your Program

  Before starting your visa application, you need to research and select a U.S. institution and program that aligns with your academic goals. Ensure the institution is SEVP (Student and Exchange Visitor Program) certified. You can select course based on your previous academic background or your field of interest. Similarly, you can select university based on different parameters like ranking, scholarship provided, location, graduates employment percentage, student support services, etc. research US institutions, SEVP certified programs, study in USA 2024, Nepali students abroad

Step 2: Apply to U.S. Institutions

  Apply to the chosen U.S. institutions. You can apply online from university website. You need to fill all your details along with the documents (academic documents, IELTS/PTE English Scorecard, Passport, Letter of Recommendations, Bank Balance Certificate, etc.). Ensure you meet all the admission requirements and deadlines. Upon acceptance, you will receive an I-20 form from the institution. It may take 1 to 2 weeks. Some university may take longer. It depends on university. US university application process, admission requirements USA, I-20 form, Nepali students US universities

Step 3: Receive Your I-20 Form

  Once accepted, the institution will issue an I-20 form, which you need for your visa application. The I-20 form contains your SEVIS (Student and Exchange Visitor Information System) number. I-20 form, SEVIS number, F-1 visa requirements, study visa USA 2024

Step 4: Pay the SEVIS Fee

  Before you can apply for a visa, you must pay the SEVIS I-901 fee. This fee supports the Student and Exchange Visitor Information System. You can pay once you receive your I-20 or 1 week before your interview date. You have to pay USD 350 as a SEVIS I-901 fee. SEVIS fee payment, I-901 fee, SEVIS fee for Nepali students

Step 5: Complete the DS-160 Form

  Fill out the DS-160 form, the online nonimmigrant visa application form. Ensure you complete all sections accurately. You will need to upload a passport-sized photo and provide details from your I-20 form. Keep your DS -160 Confirmation page handy, you need to take a copy of your confirmation page while attending for a visa interview. DS-160 form, nonimmigrant visa application, DS-160 form guide, US visa application form

Step 6: Schedule Your Visa Interview

  Schedule an appointment for your visa interview at the U.S. Embassy in Nepal. You can book you interview date via CGI Fedral website. Register and fill all the details. You need to pay Visa fee that is USD 185 which is equivalent to NPR 24,475. Be prepared to choose a convenient date and time for your interview. schedule visa interview, US embassy Nepal, US student visa interview, visa appointment scheduling

Step 7: Attend the Visa Interview

  Attend your visa interview with all necessary documents, including your passport, DS-160 confirmation page, visa appointment confirmation, I-20 form, SEVIS fee receipt, and financial documents. Be prepared to answer questions about your study plans, institution choice, and post-graduation plans. Once visa interview is completed, your visa decision whether approved or rejected will convey to you by a visa officer. US visa interview tips, required documents for US visa, student visa interview questions, visa interview preparation

Step 8: Receive Your Visa and Prepare for Departure

  If your visa is approved, you will receive your passport with the visa stamp. Prepare for your departure by booking your flight, arranging accommodation, and familiarizing yourself with U.S. customs and regulations. US visa approval, travel to USA, pre-departure checklist for US-bound students, student visa USA 2024
Are you interested to study in Canada, if yes, this article might be helpful for you. Click this link.

Tips for a Successful USA Student Visa Process and Application

  - Start Early: Begin your application process as early as possible to avoid last-minute issues. - Organize Your Documents: Ensure all your documents are complete and organized. - Practice Your Interview: Be clear and confident during your visa interview. Practice common interview questions. - Show Strong Ties to Nepal: Demonstrate that you have reasons to return to Nepal after your studies, such as family, property, or job prospects. US visa application tips, successful student visa application, visa interview preparation, documents for US visa

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

  Q: How long does the visa process take? A: The visa process can take several weeks to a few months. Start early to ensure timely completion. Q: What if my visa is denied? A: If your visa is denied, you can reapply. Address the reasons for denial before reapplying. Q: Can I work while studying on an F-1 visa? A: Yes, F-1 visa holders can work on-campus and apply for Optional Practical Training (OPT) for off-campus work after completing their studies. student visa processing time, visa denial, work on F-1 visa, OPT for F-1 visa holders

Conclusion

  Securing a USA student visa is a multi-step process that requires careful planning and preparation. By following this guide, Nepali students can navigate each stage confidently and increase their chances of success. Remember to start early, stay organized, and prepare thoroughly for your visa interview. For more updates and detailed guides on studying abroad, stay tuned to our blog! USA student visa guide, study abroad 2024, Nepali students in USA, student visa application steps --- This guide covers the complete process for Nepali students applying for a USA student visa in 2024, with detailed steps and tips to ensure a successful application. Use this information to make your dream of studying in the United States a reality!

item.title: How to Fill DS-160 Form Correctly: Step-by-Step Guide
item.dc:creator: bipin.sharma
item.content:encoded:
Applying for a U.S. visa can be a daunting task, but filling out the DS-160 form correctly is crucial for a smooth application process. This comprehensive guide will walk you through each step, ensuring you complete the form accurately and efficiently. By following these steps, you can avoid common mistakes and increase your chances of a successful visa application. How to Fill DS-160 Form Correctly YOUTUBE video step by step: [embed]https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Q2B0CeuNMQc&t=465s[/embed]

What is the DS-160 Form?

  The DS-160, also known as the Online Nonimmigrant Visa Application, is required for anyone applying for a nonimmigrant visa to the United States. This form collects personal, travel, and background information to determine your eligibility for a U.S. visa.

Before You Start: Gather Necessary Information

  Before you begin filling out the DS-160 form, ensure you have the following information and documents:
  1. Passport: Your passport details, including passport number, issuance date, and expiration date.
  2. Travel itinerary: Dates and details of your planned travel to the U.S. 3. Previous U.S. travel information: Dates of prior visits to the U.S., if any. 4. U.S. contact information: Details of your contact person or organization in the U.S. 5. Employment history: Information about your current and previous employment. 6. Educational background: Details of your educational institutions and qualifications. 7. Digital photo: A recent photo that meets U.S. visa requirements.

Step-by-Step Guide to Filling Out the DS-160 Form

 

Step 1: Access the DS-160 Form

  1. Visit the [Consular Electronic Application Center (CEAC) website](https://ceac.state.gov/genniv/). 2. Select the location where you will be applying for your visa and start your application. 3. Note down the Application ID displayed on the top right corner of the page. This ID is crucial for retrieving your application if you need to save and continue later.

Step 2: Personal Information

  1. Full Name: Enter your full name as it appears on your passport. 2. Other Names: If you have used any other names, such as a maiden name, list them. 3. Marital Status: Select your current marital status. 4. Nationality: Choose your nationality from the dropdown menu.

Step 3: Travel Information

  1. Purpose of Trip to the U.S.: Select the appropriate visa category. 2. Intended Date of Arrival: Enter your planned arrival date. 3. Address Where You Will Stay: Provide the address of your hotel, relative, or friend in the U.S.

Step 4: Travel Companions

  1. Traveling with Anyone: Indicate if you are traveling with anyone and provide their details if applicable.

Step 5: Previous U.S. Travel

  1. Previous U.S. Visits: Enter information about any previous visits to the U.S. 2. Visa Denials: Indicate if you have ever been denied a U.S. visa.

Step 6: U.S. Contact Information

  1. Contact Person or Organization: Provide the name and contact details of your U.S. contact. 2. Relationship to You: Specify your relationship to this person or organization.

Step 7: Family Information

  1. Parents’ Names: Enter the names of your parents. 2. Spouse’s Information: If applicable, provide details about your spouse.

Step 8: Work/Education/Training Information

  1. Current Employment: Provide details about your current job, including your employer's name and address. 2. Previous Employment: List your previous employers, if any. 3. Education: Enter details about your educational background.

Step 9: Security and Background Information

  1. Security Questions: Answer a series of questions related to your health, criminal history, and security concerns. Answer honestly and accurately.

Step 10: Review and Confirm

  1. Review Your Information: Carefully review all the information you have entered to ensure it is correct. 2. Confirm and Submit: After confirming the accuracy of your information, submit the form.

Step 11: Upload Your Photo

  1. Photo Requirements: Ensure your photo meets the [U.S. visa photo requirements](https://travel.state.gov/content/travel/en/us-visas/visa-information-resources/photos.html). 2. Upload Photo: Upload your photo and ensure it is correctly displayed on the form.

Step 12: Print the Confirmation Page

  1. Confirmation Page: After successfully submitting your DS-160 form, print the confirmation page with the barcode. This page is required for your visa interview.

Common Mistakes to Avoid

  1. Incorrect Information: Double-check all entries to avoid errors. 2. Incomplete Form: Ensure all required fields are filled out. 3. Inconsistent Details: Make sure the information on your DS-160 form matches your other application documents.

Conclusion

  Filling out the DS-160 form correctly is a crucial step in the U.S. visa application process. By following this detailed guide, you can ensure that your application is accurate and complete, increasing your chances of a successful visa interview. Remember to review your information carefully and print the confirmation page for your records. Good luck with your U.S. visa application! --- By following this guide, you should be well-prepared to complete the DS-160 form accurately. For more detailed information, visit the [U.S. Department of State's website](https://travel.state.gov/content/travel/en/us-visas.html).

item.title: Study and Work in Lithuania as an International Student: A Comprehensive Guide
item.dc:creator: bipin.sharma
item.content:encoded:
Lithuania, a Baltic gem, is becoming an increasingly popular destination for international students seeking quality education and diverse work opportunities. With its rich cultural heritage, vibrant cities, and affordable living costs, Lithuania offers a unique blend of traditional charm and modern conveniences. This article aims to provide a detailed guide for international students considering studying and working in Lithuania.

Why Choose Lithuania for Higher Education?

Quality Education

Lithuania is home to several reputable universities and colleges that offer a wide range of programs in English. Institutions like Vilnius University, Kaunas University of Technology, and Vytautas Magnus University are renowned for their academic excellence and research facilities. Lithuanian universities follow the European Credit Transfer and Accumulation System (ECTS), ensuring that the degrees awarded are recognized across Europe and beyond.

Affordable Tuition Fees

Compared to many Western countries, the cost of education in Lithuania is relatively low. Tuition fees for international students can range from €1,000 to €5,000 per year, depending on the program and the university. Scholarships and financial aid options are also available to help ease the financial burden.

Cultural Diversity and Welcoming Environment

Lithuania is known for its warm hospitality and inclusive environment. International students will find a diverse community with various cultural and social activities that facilitate integration and foster a sense of belonging. The country’s strategic location also allows easy travel to other European countries, enriching the overall experience.

High Quality of Life

Lithuania offers a high standard of living at a fraction of the cost compared to Western Europe. The cost of living, including accommodation, food, and transportation, is significantly lower, making it an attractive destination for students. The country is also known for its safety, with low crime rates and a stable political environment.

Higher Education System in Lithuania

 

Types of Institutions

Lithuania’s higher education system comprises universities and colleges. Universities focus on academic research and offer bachelor’s, master’s, and doctoral programs. Colleges, on the other hand, provide professional education and are more practice-oriented, offering undergraduate programs.

Popular Programs

Lithuanian universities offer a diverse range of programs in fields such as business, engineering, information technology, medicine, and social sciences. Some of the popular programs among international students include: - Business Administration - Computer Science - Medicine - International Relations - Engineering

Admission Requirements

Admission requirements vary depending on the institution and the program. Generally, international students need to provide the following: - Completed application form - Academic transcripts - Proof of English proficiency (IELTS, TOEFL, or equivalent) - Motivation letter - Recommendation letters - Passport copy

Application Process

The application process typically involves submitting the required documents online through the university’s admission portal. It is advisable to apply early and ensure that all documents are in order. Some universities may also require an entrance examination or an interview.

Living in Lithuania as an International Student

Accommodation

Most universities in Lithuania offer dormitory accommodation to international students. Dormitory living is a cost-effective option, with prices ranging from €50 to €150 per month. Alternatively, students can opt for private rentals, which can cost between €200 and €500 per month, depending on the location and type of accommodation.

Cost of Living

The cost of living in Lithuania is relatively low compared to other European countries. On average, international students can expect to spend around €400 to €700 per month, covering accommodation, food, transportation, and other expenses. Here’s a breakdown of typical monthly expenses: - Accommodation: €100 - €400 - Food: €100 - €200 - Transportation: €10 - €20 - Utilities and Internet: €50 - €100 - Leisure and entertainment: €50 - €100

Health Insurance

International students are required to have health insurance during their stay in Lithuania. Many universities offer health insurance plans for students, or they can opt for private health insurance. The cost of health insurance can range from €100 to €300 per year, depending on the coverage.

Transportation

Lithuania has an efficient public transportation system, including buses, trolleybuses, and trains. Students can avail of discounted fares by purchasing monthly or semester passes. Biking is also a popular and eco-friendly mode of transport in many Lithuanian cities.

Cultural and Social Life

Lithuania is rich in cultural heritage, with numerous festivals, museums, and historical sites to explore. The country’s vibrant cities, such as Vilnius, Kaunas, and Klaipėda, offer a lively social scene with cafes, restaurants, and clubs. Student organizations and clubs are active on university campuses, providing opportunities to engage in various extracurricular activities and make new friends.

Working in Lithuania as an International Student

Part-Time Work Opportunities

International students in Lithuania are allowed to work part-time during their studies. The Lithuanian law permits students to work up to 20 hours per week during the academic year and full-time during holidays. This provides an excellent opportunity to gain work experience and support oneself financially.

Popular Part-Time Jobs

Common part-time jobs for international students include positions in retail, hospitality, and administrative roles. Many universities also offer on-campus job opportunities, such as research assistantships, tutoring, and library jobs. Knowledge of the Lithuanian language can be an advantage, but there are also plenty of English-speaking job opportunities available.
Popular Jobs Teaching Assistant, Retail Assistant, Delivery Rider, Baristas etc.  
Work Hours 
  • 40 hours per week for EU students; 20 hours/week for Non-EU students. 
  • Non-EU students can work full-time if they have a temporary residence permit. 
  • Ph.D. students can work full-time regardless of nationality. 
Where to Find Jobs  Online Job Portals, personal networks, university career centers, etc. 
Average Earning  964 EUR/ Month (Minimum Wage)
Teaching Assistant: This on-campus role is typically available within various university departments. Teaching Assistants (TAs) are responsible for supporting professors with instructional duties, which may include grading assignments, leading discussion sections, and providing academic assistance to students. Research Assistant: Research Assistants support faculty members’ research projects, often within the student’s field of study. This role involves tasks such as data collection, analysis, and literature reviews, providing valuable experience in academic research methodologies. Barista/Café Worker: Off-campus barista or café worker positions involve preparing and serving beverages, such as coffee and tea, as well as snacks. These roles require excellent customer service skills and the ability to work in a fast-paced environment. Library Monitor: Library Monitors play a crucial role in managing the circulation of books and ensuring that the library environment remains conducive to study. They may also assist students in locating resources and maintaining the organization of library materials. IT Support: IT Support staff on campus help resolve technical issues for students and faculty, maintain computer labs, and ensure the smooth operation of the university’s IT infrastructure. They may also assist with software installations and network troubleshooting. Tour Guide: Knowledgeable about the local area, Tour Guides lead groups of visitors through attractions, providing interesting information and answering questions. This job is ideal for those who enjoy interacting with people and have a passion for sharing their local culture. Retail Assistant: Retail Assistants work in various shops and are involved in sales transactions, customer service, and stocking shelves. They must be knowledgeable about the products they sell and adept at handling different types of customers. Bartender/Waitstaff: Working as a Bartender or Waitstaff in restaurants and bars is a common evening job for students. These roles involve serving food and drinks, managing customer orders, and ensuring a pleasant dining experience. Customer Service Representative: Customer Service Representatives handle customer inquiries and complaints, often in call centers or online support platforms. Some positions may offer the flexibility of remote work, allowing employees to assist customers from home. Online Tutor: Online Tutors provide instruction in languages or other subjects to students across the globe via the Internet. This role requires strong communication skills and a thorough understanding of the subject matter being taught. It’s a great way to connect with learners from diverse backgrounds and make a positive impact on their education.

Work Permits

International students from non-EU countries need a temporary residence permit to study in Lithuania. This permit also allows them to work part-time. It is important to ensure that the employer provides a proper employment contract and that the working hours do not interfere with academic commitments.

How Much Can International Students Earn in Lithuania?

The average monthly income in Lithuania is about 1,666.9 EUR. Part-time working students generally earn less than this average because of the limited hours they are allowed to work. Wages for part-time jobs can vary widely, typically around or slightly above the minimum wage. As of the first quarter of 2024, the minimum wage in Lithuania is 924 EUR per month. It’s important to recognize that salaries can vary significantly across different sectors and industries. Non-EU students can stay in Lithuania for an additional year after graduation to seek employment. During this time, they can work full-time and may earn an average wage or potentially more, depending on the job market conditions and their qualifications. The personal income tax rate in Lithuania is 20% for monthly earnings below 7,520.50 EUR and 32% for incomes exceeding this amount.

Internships and Career Opportunities

Lithuania’s growing economy and favorable business environment offer numerous internship and career opportunities for international students. Many multinational companies have established their presence in Lithuania, particularly in the fields of information technology, finance, and engineering. Universities often have career centers that assist students in finding internships and job placements, providing valuable support for career development.

Post-Graduation Employment

Upon graduation, international students can apply for a temporary residence permit for job search purposes, which is valid for one year. This allows graduates to stay in Lithuania and look for employment opportunities. If a graduate secures a job, they can then apply for a work permit and extend their stay.

Tips for Finding Jobs for International Students in Lithuania   

Understand Visa Regulations

Before looking for employment, it's essential to understand the visa regulations for international students in Lithuania. Some visas may limit the number of hours students can work during the academic term, while others may require a work permit.

Utilize University Resources

Many Lithuanian universities offer career services and job placement assistance for their students. These resources often include job fairs, career counseling, and internship opportunities tailored to international students.

Networking

Networking is crucial in Lithuania, as it is elsewhere. Attend networking events, workshops, and seminars to connect with professionals in your field. Joining student clubs and organizations can also provide valuable networking opportunities.

Language Skills

Although many Lithuanians speak English, proficiency in the Lithuanian language can greatly improve your job prospects, especially for roles involving direct interaction with local clients or customers. Consider taking language courses to enhance your language skills.

Online Job Portals

Explore Lithuanian-specific online job portals such as cv.lt, cvonline.lt, and workinlithuania.lt. These platforms list job vacancies across various industries and sectors, including internships and part-time positions suitable for students.

Internships and Traineeships

Internships and traineeships are excellent ways for international students to gain work experience and build professional networks in Lithuania. Many companies offer internships to students, providing valuable insights into the local job market.

Freelancing and Remote Work

With the increase in remote work opportunities, international students can explore freelancing platforms to find remote job opportunities in Lithuania or with international companies. Websites like Upwork, Freelancer, and Fiverr offer a wide range of freelance gigs.

Work in International Companies

Some international companies operating in Lithuania prefer hiring English-speaking employees, creating job opportunities for international students. Research multinational companies with a presence in Lithuania and inquire about job openings or internship programs.

Work in the Education Sector

International students with relevant qualifications and language skills may find employment opportunities in the education sector, such as language teaching or tutoring positions.

Legal Compliance

Ensure that any job you apply for complies with Lithuanian labor laws and regulations. Be aware of your rights as an international student employee, including minimum wage requirements and working hour restrictions.

Visa and Residence Permit Process

Visa Requirements

International students from non-EU countries need a national visa (D) to enter Lithuania for study purposes. The visa application process typically requires the following documents: - Valid passport - University acceptance letter - Proof of sufficient funds - Health insurance - Completed visa application form - Passport-sized photographs

Temporary Residence Permit

Upon arrival in Lithuania, international students need to apply for a temporary residence permit, which is valid for one year and can be renewed annually. The application process involves submitting the required documents to the Migration Department. It is advisable to apply for the residence permit as soon as possible after arriving in Lithuania.

Tips for Success as an International Student in Lithuania

Learn the Language

While many Lithuanians speak English, learning the basics of the Lithuanian language can greatly enhance your experience and help you integrate into the local community. Many universities offer Lithuanian language courses for international students.

Engage in Extracurricular Activities

Participating in extracurricular activities, such as joining student organizations, clubs, and sports teams, can help you build a network, make friends, and enrich your overall experience. It also provides an opportunity to develop new skills and interests.

Utilize University Resources

Take advantage of the resources available at your university, such as academic advising, career counseling, and health services. These resources are designed to support your academic and personal development.

Explore the Country

Lithuania is a beautiful country with a rich history and diverse landscapes. Take the time to explore its cities, national parks, and cultural sites. Traveling within Lithuania and neighboring countries can be a rewarding experience and provide a deeper understanding of the region.

Manage Your Finances

Budgeting and managing your finances effectively is crucial for a successful student life. Keep track of your expenses, take advantage of student discounts, and find part-time work opportunities to support yourself financially.

Conclusion

Lithuania offers a unique and enriching experience for international students, with its high-quality education, affordable living costs, and vibrant cultural scene. Whether you are seeking academic excellence, career opportunities, or a new cultural adventure, Lithuania has much to offer. By understanding the higher education system, living conditions, work opportunities, and visa requirements, you can make an informed decision and embark on a successful academic journey in Lithuania. Studying and working in Lithuania as an international student can be a life-changing experience, opening doors to new opportunities and broadening your horizons. Embrace the challenges and opportunities that come your way and make the most of your time in this beautiful Baltic country.

item.title: UK Student Visa from Nepal: Complete Guide
item.dc:creator: bipin.sharma
item.content:encoded:
Ultimate Guide to UK Student Visa from Nepal (2025 Edition)

  YouTube VIDEO: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2wq9mIcAmg0

Introduction to UK Student Visa from Nepal for Nepali Students

The UK and the UK student visa from Nepal remains one of the most sought-after destinations and concern for Nepali students pursuing higher education abroad. Its world-class universities, multicultural environment, and generous post-study work options make it a top choice. From London to Edinburgh, Nepali students can explore a vast range of academic programs while experiencing British culture firsthand. Many students choose the UK for its:
  • Globally recognized degrees
  • Shorter course durations (3-year undergraduate and 1-year postgraduate)
  • Access to top research facilities and job opportunities
Popular courses among Nepali students include:
  • Business and Management
  • Engineering and IT
  • Health and Social Care
  • Hospitality and Tourism
  • Law and Humanities
In this guide, we’ll explore everything you need to know about applying for a UK student visa from Nepal, including the process, documents, financial requirements, and more.

Types of UK Student Visa from Nepal for Nepali Citizens

Nepali students have several visa options depending on their age and course type.

Tier 4 (General) Student Visa

Now known as the Student Route Visa, this is the most common for Nepali students aged 16 or above studying full-time courses.

Short-term Study Visa

Ideal for English language courses lasting 6–11 months. This visa doesn’t allow work and is not extendable.

Child Student Visa

For students aged 4–17 attending a UK independent school. Each visa type has its own requirements, duration, and rights, so it's crucial to choose the right one based on your academic goals.

Basic Eligibility Criteria

Before applying, ensure you meet the following requirements: Academic Qualification: You must be accepted into a UK institution with a valid Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies (CAS). English Proficiency: Typically proven through IELTS, TOEFL, or PTE scores. Financial Capability: Must show proof of sufficient funds to cover tuition and living expenses. Valid Passport: With at least 6 months of validity. You must also be at least 16 years old and have no criminal convictions that disqualify you from UK entry.

Step-by-Step Application Process

Here’s a clear breakdown of how Nepali students can apply for a UK student visa in 2025: Research & Choose Your Course Select a UK university approved by the UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI). Receive CAS Letter After getting accepted, the university sends a CAS letter with a unique reference number. Create an Online Visa Application Complete your application at gov.uk. Pay Visa & Health Fees Includes the visa application fee and Immigration Health Surcharge (IHS). Book a Biometric Appointment Schedule your appointment at the UK Visa Application Centre at VFS in Kathmandu. Attend Interview (if applicable) UKVI may invite you for a credibility interview. Wait for a Decision Processing usually takes 3 weeks but can be faster with priority service.

Documents Required for UK Student Visa from Nepal

Prepare the following essential documents:
Document Description
Valid Passport Minimum 6 months validity
CAS Letter Provided by the UK university
Financial Proof Bank statements, loan letters, sponsor affidavits
TB Test Certificate From a UK-approved clinic in Nepal
English Test Results IELTS, TOEFL iBT, or PTE Academic
Academic Transcripts +2, bachelor’s, or master’s results
Birth Certificate (for minors) Required for students under 18
All documents must be in English or accompanied by official translations.

Financial Requirements Explained

Understanding the financial criteria is key to avoiding a visa refusal: Tuition Fees: Varies by course and university (typically £10,000–£25,000 per year). Living Costs: London: £1,334/month (up to 9 months) = £12,006 Outside London: £1,023/month = £9,207 Your financial documents must show these amounts maintained for at least 28 consecutive days. Acceptable financial proofs include:
  • Personal bank statements
  • Education loans from recognized banks
  • Fixed deposits (with encashment proof)
  • Sponsor’s bank statements and relationship proof

English Language Requirements

Most UK universities require proof of English proficiency. Accepted tests include:
Test Minimum Score
IELTS Academic 6.0 overall (no band < 5.5)
TOEFL iBT 80+
PTE Academic 50+
Some institutions waive this requirement for students who studied in English medium schools, subject to conditions (B or B+ in Grade 12 English)

How to Get a Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies (CAS)

The CAS is a unique reference number issued by your university after admission. CAS Validity: 6 months from the date of issue. Issuance Time: Typically, 4–8 weeks after unconditional offer. Importance: Required before applying for a student visa. Make sure the details on your CAS are accurate, as discrepancies can lead to visa delays or refusal.

Visa Application Fees and Healthcare Surcharge

As of 2025, the costs include: Student Visa Fee: £490 (approx. NPR 87,000) Immigration Health Surcharge (IHS): £776 per year (for access to NHS services) Payment is made online via the official visa application portal.

Biometrics and Visa Interview Preparation

After submitting your application: Biometrics: Book and attend an appointment at the UK Visa Application Centre in Kathmandu. Interview (if required): Be prepared to explain:
  • Why you chose the UK and your course
  • Funding sources
  • Career plans after graduation
Always answer truthfully and confidently.

Common Reasons for Visa Rejection

Understanding common pitfalls helps in avoiding them:
  • Insufficient Financial Documents
  • Invalid CAS or Mismatched Details
  • Unclear Study Intentions
  • Low English Test Scores
  • Unrealistic Education History
Even small errors can lead to rejections, so double-check all documents and answers.

How to Avoid UK student Visa Refusal from Nepal

To boost your success rate:
  • Keep a strong financial record (with 28-day balance proof).
  • Practice for the credibility interview.
  • Submit only genuine and complete documents.
  • Ensure your CAS and personal information match.
  • Clearly explain your academic and career goals.
Consulting with a verified education advisor in Nepal can also help.

Life in the UK as a Nepali Student

Living in the UK can be both exciting and challenging. Here’s what to expect:
  • Part-time Work: Allowed up to 20 hours/week during term and full-time during holidays.
  • Accommodation: Choose from university halls, private rentals, or homestays.
  • Community: Active Nepali student associations offer support and social events.
  • Cultural Adaptation: Embrace diversity, learn local customs, and stay connected with home via community events.

Post-Study Work Opportunities

The UK offers attractive post-study options:
  • Graduate Route Visa: Stay in the UK for 2 years (3 for PhDs) after graduation to work or look for jobs.
  • Work Visas: Skilled Worker visa if you get a job with a licensed sponsor.
  • Entrepreneur Options: Start-up and Innovator visas for aspiring business owners.

Dependents and Family Visa Options

You can bring your spouse and children if:
  • You’re studying a postgraduate course of 9+ months at a UK university
  • You can financially support them without public funds
Dependents can work full-time in the UK, adding financial stability for families.

Role of Educational Consultancies in Nepal

Many students use educational consultancies to simplify the process. Services include:
  • University selection and application
  • Visa documentation support
  • Pre-departure briefing
Top Consultancies in Nepal:
  • Central College of Vocational Training Pvt. Ltd.
  • 056-594273

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

1. How long does it take to get a UK student visa from Nepal? Usually 3 weeks after biometrics, but faster options are available. 2. Can I work while studying in the UK? Yes, up to 20 hours per week during term and full-time during breaks. 3. What is the success rate of UK student visa from Nepal? Over 95% with correct documentation and genuine study intent. 4. Do I need a TB test for UK visa from Nepal? Yes, from an approved clinic by UKVI. 5. Can I bring my spouse and children with a student visa? Yes, if enrolled in a postgraduate course longer than 9 months. 6. What happens if my visa is refused? You may reapply or appeal, depending on the reason for refusal.

Conclusion: Final Checklist for a Successful Application

Before you apply, make sure to: ✅ Choose a UKVI-approved university ✅ Receive your CAS letter ✅ Prepare accurate financial and academic documents ✅ Take an approved English test ✅ Pay visa and IHS fees ✅ Attend your biometric appointment ✅ Be ready for an interview if required With proper planning and preparation, your dream of studying in the UK can become a reality.

item.title: Australian Student Visa Checklist for Nepalese Students 2025
item.dc:creator: bipin.sharma
item.content:encoded:
Top 17 Reasons to Study in Australia: Insider Tips, Costs & Visa Guide

Study in Australia with confidence! Discover top universities, visa tips, tuition fees, and student life insights in this detailed 2025 guide.

1. Introduction

Australia is one of the most popular destinations for international students, and for good reason. With its world-class universities, stunning landscapes, multicultural society, and post-study work opportunities, it’s no surprise students from over 190 countries choose to study in Australia each year. From the vibrant city life of Melbourne and Sydney to the laid-back charm of Brisbane and Perth, Australia offers an enriching academic and cultural experience. Whether you're looking to gain a globally recognized degree or expand your career prospects, studying in Australia is a life-changing decision.

2. Benefits of Studying in Australia

Australia's education system ranks among the best globally. Here’s why students flock Down Under: High-Quality Education: Australian universities consistently rank in the top 100 worldwide. Global Recognition: Australian qualifications are respected by employers and academic institutions worldwide. Innovative Teaching: Institutions focus on research, creativity, and critical thinking. Lifestyle: Beaches, forests, deserts, and cities—Australia has it all. Work Rights: Students can work up to 48 hours per fortnight during studies.

3. Top Universities in Australia

Here are the most sought-after institutions for international students:
University World Ranking (2025)
University of Melbourne #14
Australian National University (ANU) #17
University of Sydney #18
University of Queensland (UQ) #23
Monash University #31
Each of these universities offers cutting-edge facilities, strong global partnerships, and supportive international student programs.

4. Most Popular Courses for International Students

Australia’s education sector is broad, but the following courses stand out for their demand and career value:
  • Business and Management
  • Engineering and IT
  • Health and Medical Sciences
  • Environmental Sciences
  • Design and Creative Arts
These courses are aligned with the Australian skilled migration list, increasing your chances of staying in the country after graduation.

5. Admission Requirements

To apply to Australian universities, you’ll need to meet these key requirements:
  • Academic Transcripts: Minimum GPA or equivalent marks.
  • English Proficiency: IELTS (6.0–7.0), TOEFL, or PTE scores.
  • Personal Statement or SOP
  • Letters of Recommendation
  • Portfolio (for creative courses)
It’s recommended to apply 6–12 months in advance for major intakes: February and July.

6. Student Visa Process (Subclass 500)

The Student Visa Subclass 500 allows full-time study and part-time work:

Step-by-step Visa Process

  1. Enroll in a CRICOS-registered course.
  2. Gather documents (COE, OSHC, passport, GTE statement).
  3. Submit visa application via ImmiAccount.
  4. Pay visa fee (~AUD $710).
  5. Wait for approval (processing time: 4–6 weeks).

7. Cost of Studying in Australia

Expense Estimated Cost (AUD/year)
Tuition Fees $20,000–$45,000
Living Expenses $21,000–$25,000
Health Insurance (OSHC) $600–$800
Student Visa Fee $710
Cities like Melbourne and Sydney are pricier, while Adelaide and Brisbane are more budget-friendly.

8. Scholarships for International Students

There are hundreds of scholarships available for merit-based or need-based applicants:
  • Australia Awards Scholarships (Government)
  • Destination Australia Program
  • University-specific Grants
  • Research Training Program (RTP)
Apply early—competition is tough!

9. Life as an International Student in Australia

Australia is culturally diverse, welcoming, and full of exciting experiences:
  • Join multicultural clubs and societies.
  • Attend festivals, sports, and local events.
  • Connect through support services and international student hubs.
This inclusive environment helps ease culture shock and fosters a sense of belonging.

10. Best Cities for Students

City Highlight
Melbourne Ranked #1 for student experience
Sydney Financial hub with top universities
Brisbane Affordable living, great weather
Perth Relaxed vibe and beautiful beaches
Adelaide Budget-friendly and student-focused
Each city has excellent public transport, nightlife, and academic infrastructure.

11. Part-Time Work Opportunities

Students on Subclass 500 can work:
  • 48 hours per fortnight during semesters
  • Unlimited hours during semester breaks
Popular jobs: retail, hospitality, tutoring, administration, delivery. Wages range from AUD $23 to $30 per hour depending on experience and location.

12. Post-Study Work Visa & PR Pathways

Graduates can apply for the Temporary Graduate Visa (Subclass 485) to work after completing their studies:
  • Duration: 2–4 years depending on course level and region.
  • PR Options: Skills assessment, employer sponsorship, regional nominations.
Australia’s migration system favors graduates in fields like IT, Engineering, Nursing, and Teaching.

13. Accommodation Options

Type Monthly Cost (AUD)
On-campus $600–$1000
Off-campus shared $400–$800
Homestay $700–$1200
Private apartment $1000–$1800
Most universities offer help with accommodation placement and legal advice.

14. Safety and Healthcare for Students

  • OSHC (Overseas Student Health Cover) is mandatory.
  • Emergency services: Call 000
  • Universities offer mental health and wellbeing support.
Australia is ranked as one of the safest countries for international students globally.

15. Cultural Tips and Australian Etiquette

G'day = Hello Don’t tip unless you want to Respect personal space and time Aussies love BBQs, beaches, and sports Understanding basic slang and local habits can help you settle in quickly.

16. Common Challenges Faced by Students

Homesickness: Join student groups and stay connected with family. Finding Jobs: Start early, use LinkedIn and job boards. Scams: Avoid deals that sound too good to be true; seek legal advice from universities. Support is always available through student services, embassies, and community groups.

17. Final Tips for Studying in Australia

  • Start applications early
  • Maintain valid documents
  • Join orientation events
  • Explore beyond campus
  • Respect visa rules
Planning wisely can help you make the most of your academic journey in Australia.

???? Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

1. Is Australia good for international students? Yes, it offers quality education, post-study work rights, scholarships, and cultural diversity. 2. What is the IELTS score required for studying in Australia? Most universities require a minimum score of 6.0 to 7.0, depending on the program. 3. Can international students work in Australia while studying? Yes, you can work up to 48 hours per fortnight during your course and full-time during breaks. 4. How much money is required to study in Australia? Roughly AUD $30,000 to $50,000 per year, including tuition, living, and visa costs. 5. How long can I stay in Australia after studying? You can stay 2–4 years on a Temporary Graduate Visa (Subclass 485). 6. Do I need health insurance in Australia? Yes, Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC) is mandatory for all international students.

Dear Sir/Madam,   We would like to invite you to attend the launch of our project “Fablab Nepal Builds STEAM for Youth” that will be held on 15 Ashoj 2078 from 11: 00 AM to 01:00 PM at Fablab Nepal. Your presence will be beyond valuable to us.   Nepal Communitere in collaboration with Karkhana aims to increase access to Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts and Mathematics (STEAM) for Community and Government Schools students and teachers. As part of the project we will be working with different schools in Fablab Nepal through
  1. A series of half day workshops for students on different topics around hands-on STEAM education
    1. Selected students will be able to attend 8 week long sessions
  2. Establish makerspaces and STEAM clubs at 5 selected schools
  3. 4 week long teacher development program for 45 teachers 
  The project is being supported by the US embassy in Nepal and  .   The launch will start with the tour of Fablab Nepal followed by a presentation about the program and integrating STEAM methodology into our classrooms.   This is an opportunity for all of us to meet, learn more about Fablab Nepal and our project. You will also be able to register your interest for our teachers and students to participate in different sessions to be conducted in the project.    We sincerely hope that you will be able to confirm your attendance at this invitation on or before 13 Ashoj 2078 by contacting us at +977-9851278038 or emailing us at nepalfablab@gmail.com. We will be happy to host one other member from your school for the event.   Hoping for your presence on that day. We look forward to meeting you.   Yours Sincerely,
